name: Gluttony (gula) as capital vice
plainSummary: In this tradition, gluttony is not only eating too much: it is inordinate desire in the realm of food and drink—quantity, delicacy, or ritual that disorders health, sobriety, or solidarity.
description: Derived principle: gula (gluttony) is the capital vice of intemperance in eating and drinking—classically including excessive concern for costly or refined fare, not merely caloric excess.
foundationStrengthRationale: Temperance language remains intelligible in public health; gourmet culture and eating disorders complicate simple labeling.

pros.claim: Connects individual appetite to stewardship of health and shared meals as moral practice.
pros.evidence: Public health ethics and environmental food ethics echo concerns about excess and waste.

cons.claim: Risk of stigmatizing body size or poverty when the term gluttony is used loosely.
cons.evidence: Critics note that metabolic, economic, and psychological factors challenge one-size moral judgments about eating.
